themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK versus a 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting a sudden animal control enforcement gap or seasonal shift in Flatlands/Canarsie.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Pattern emergence within last 7 days suggests acute trigger, not seasonal trend
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Animal Care and Control about staffing and response times in CD 318
Canvass residents near complaint addresses about safety concerns and enforcement visibility

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—a 2300% surge (z-score: 8.69, highest severity spike in dataset)—indicating potential organized posting or enforcement collapse in storefronts and public spaces.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase)
Highest z-score in dataset at 8.69—most anomalous complaint type
Baseline of near-zero complaints suggests either new enforcement detection or sudden posting activity
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if posting is concentrated in specific commercial corridors (Flatbush Ave, etc.)
Contact Sanitation Department to learn if they've increased complaints intake or if posting activity genuinely spiked

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 22 LAST WEEK versus a 5.2 weekly average—a 319% increase (z-score: 3.29)—coinciding with vehicle noise complaints at 11 two weeks ago (226% above baseline), suggesting construction, traffic enforcement gaps, or event activity.
evidence: 22 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 5.2 weekly average (319% spike, z-score: 3.29)
Vehicle noise at 11 complaints two weeks ago vs. 3.4 average (226% spike, z-score: 3.82)
Dual spikes in related noise categories suggest systemic cause, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits (368 total filings, 273 alterations) to identify active construction projects generating complaints
Interview residents near high-complaint zones about timing and noise sources (construction hours, delivery trucks, street vendors)

themes_detail.label: Curb and Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints reached 10 LAST WEEK versus a 2.5 weekly baseline—a 300% spike (z-score: 4.33)—indicating rapid sidewalk/curb damage, likely driven by freeze-thaw cycles or deferred maintenance exacerbated by recent snow complaints (943 over 90 days).
evidence: 10 curb condition complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 4.33)
943 snow/ice complaints over 90 days suggests winter damage to infrastructure
Street condition is also a top-10 complaint type overall (563 over 90 days), indicating systemic street maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with Sanitation and DOT on 2024 curb repair and resurfacing schedules for CD 318
Document photo essay of curb damage in high-complaint areas (map 311 data by block)

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Health Issues
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK versus 1.8 weekly average—a 186% increase (z-score: 3.36)—suggesting either increased inspections, a cluster of violations, or outbreak-related reporting in Flatlands/Canarsie dining venues.
evidence: 5 food establishment complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (186% spike, z-score: 3.36)
Baseline complaint volume suggests established venues are the subject, not new openings
Spike could signal health department enforcement push or foodborne illness cluster
reporting_angles: Query NYC Health Dept database for recent violations, critical violations, or closure actions in CD 318
Interview Health Dept about whether spike reflects increased inspections or genuine violation clustering
